title: Deep learning ECG model estimates right ventricular size and function
summary: A deep learning ECG model was trained against cardiac MRI in UK Biobank (n = 42,938), fine-tuned in Mount Sinai Hospital data (n = 3019) and prospectively validated over 4 months (n = 115). AUROCs for RV dysfunction were 0.86, 0.81 and 0.77, and for RV dilation 0.91, 0.81 and 0.92 across the three cohorts. RVEF prediction was associated with transplant-free survival. The prospective set is small and RV dysfunction prevalence was low in UK Biobank (1.0%).
ai_technology: Deep learning model on 12-lead ECG predicting RV dilation, RV dysfunction, RVEF and RVEDV against cardiac MRI
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

evidence.tested: Training in UK Biobank, fine-tuning at Mount Sinai Hospital and prospective validation over 4 months (n = 115).
evidence.unknown: Performance in larger prospective cohorts and in other health systems; clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts right ventricular volume and ejection fraction from the ECG instead of imaging.
